statement: status and manuscript converge after a merge. Two independent derivations run over one log — status is the single latest LIFECYCLE op by opId, text is a fold of every op's changes in opId order — and nothing made them agree, so a reject beating an already-spliced accept settled `rejected` with the suggestion still in the manuscript, permanently (neither reject nor reopen could move text). The post-merge pass now appends a `claudeReject` carrying the INVERSE changes, stamped `synthesisSource = .rejectConvergence` and carrying the winning reject's userResponse: one op that is both the newest lifecycle op (status stays rejected) and the newest changes-carrying op (the text goes back). `Deriver.appliesToManuscript` admits `.claudeReject` for this and only this — every writer-issued reject still carries empty changes — and ProjectManifest.currentSchemaVersion went 4→5 because an older build folds none of it. Idempotent: once the repair is the newest payload the detection is false, so two devices repairing the same race cannot ping-pong. DECLINES loudly when the paragraph has drifted since the accept, leaving the disagreement visible rather than writing over the writer's own sentences. WAITS while the piece is unsettled (#84, Denver's ruling (a), 2026-10-19): where the stamp carries `localWritePermit.unsettledStarter` — a book author's hand in a piece somebody else started and nobody has claimed — the repair writes nothing, because its text would CLAIM the piece in the author's name and set the starter's held words aside on every Mac. The disagreement stands visibly and loses nothing; the trigger persists, so a later merge repairs it once the stamp has settled (not the merge that brings the claim — DocumentStore re-stamps after handleExternalLogChange)

scope: Document.declineUndo — the annotation undos' drift declines
statement: One ⌘Z over a COALESCED batch reports its declines in ONE sentence carrying the count; a single decline reads exactly as it always has. The bulk bar registers one undo closure per note and `NSUndoManager.groupsByEvent` folds them into a single event group (pinned by `AnnotationBulkActionsTests`), and each closure re-checks its own note at fire time and declines out loud when it drifted (RULING-22, M5-AN-019's shape). Before this every declining closure called `notifyWriter` directly, so N drifted notes posted the SINGULAR sentence N times into a toast slot that renders one (`RewindModifier`'s `restoreToast = message`): the writer read 'Couldn't undo stetting the note' — false about the number, and silent about the notes that DID undo. The four decline sites (the annotation edit, the textless accept, the stet, the triage mark) now call `Document.declineUndo(_:)`, which accumulates per `UndoDecline` verb and spends one sentence a main-actor hop after the last of the batch's undo closures — RULING-32's sweep shape (`_sweptSinceLastReport`, spent at the burst boundary) applied to the same problem one column over. The boundary needs no timer: every sibling closure's task is enqueued before the report task is created, and a declining closure never suspends. Each verb's singular and plural sentences sit on adjacent lines in `UndoDecline`, and the singular is byte-identical to what each site posted before — the single-note decline tests are the proof. A batch that declined some notes and undid others says nothing about the successes: the queue holds the reopened rows. scope: Research note and palette card versions — when one is kept
statement: A Research note or palette card (a text item in Research whose path sits inside a research root — research/ or a loose piece's own research/ folder, no path component starting with '.'; a card is a direct child of the role-first palette group (`PaletteLookup.paletteCards`, so a renamed group keeps its cards; the palette folder's path prefix decides only in a manifest with no palette group at all; a document in a subgroup beneath the Palette is a note) — that role-first rule is the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's — and cards keep versions since Denver's 2026-11-11 answer to P2) keeps earlier versions under .maugham/research-versions/<itemId>/, the last 50 per item per device (a restore also spares the version it restores, M5-AN-091): the writer's own typing — in the note editor, or the card editor's own saves (updatePaletteCard(typed: true)) — keeps ONE version per editing run (saves less than 10 minutes apart are one run — the text before the run), and every other writer of a note's or card's text ALWAYS keeps what it replaced and ends the run — a canvas Rewrite (which lands only if that version was kept, and leaves no Trash entry, M6-PR-037) or link append, a canvas or inbox promotion into a card (the assistant's promote_inbox_entry marked as replaced by the assistant), a wiki-link rename sweep, a kept compiler letter (`LetterKeep.keep`: a store with its door writes the letter through it as the assistant, and it must land, so the writer's first edit of the kept note keeps it marked 'Written by assistant'; a kept letter whose save does not land throws researchTextNotSaved before anything is reported kept, and takes back the empty note it made and its chapter link, M5-AN-092), Search & Replace, an asset-reference rewrite after a rename or move, a Restore, and the assistant's update_note (notes only); a change made to the file outside Maugham is kept at the next save (an open editor hears it and reloads, M5-AN-071 and M5-AN-089). A new card's blank template (`ProjectStore.addPaletteCard`) is nobody's text: the first save over exactly those bytes keeps nothing (`ResearchNoteDoor.wroteATemplate`; the template's hash is held in the door's memory only, so a quit before the first save keeps it once on the next run; a card edited outside before its first save keeps those bytes as any others) — the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's, N8. Anything else (a table, picture, PDF, or a text item whose path is outside a research root, such as the manuscript or a .maugham/ file) is refused by the door and keeps nothing. Wherever the project's window store is open (every production writer), a note's or card's text is written only through the door — the palette funnel (paletteCoordinatedWrite) included, and every card writer reaches it; the raw write is only where no `DocumentStore` ever was (`ProjectStore.rawNoteWriteWithNoDoor()` is `.allowed` only for a store never given one — a load-only context): there the rename sweep, Replace, a promotion, a kept letter, `add_note` and the palette funnel write raw and keep no version; a store that had one and lost it (teardown) refuses instead — a writer that can throw throws `noteWriteRefusedAsTheProjectCloses`, one that cannot returns without writing, and every no-door fallback asks `rawNoteWriteWithNoDoor()` first, a counted census (`TripwireGrepTests.test_everyNoDoorFallbackAsksTheQuestion`) (the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's, N6); and, like the table door, no writer writes anything whose path is outside a research root. When anyone else's write of a card cannot keep its version, it is refused (updatePaletteCard throws researchTextNotSaved, the card is as it was, and the door says why); the card editor's own save lands with the notice, as a note's flush does. A canvas Rewrite of a text item or card outside a research root is refused before anything is read or written. When a version cannot be kept, a timed autosave is not made and the writer is told once; a save at a note switch, close, ⌘S or a move is made anyway with a notice that the earlier version could not be kept, said once and only after the save has landed, so a save that never lands says only what happened (ruled as built: Denver, 2026-11-11, P3, RULING-24's amendment; a Research table's flush follows the same rule, RULING-60, and changes with it, M5-AN-081). A file that will not read is never saved over. A timed autosave that is not made — its version cannot be kept, its file will not read, or its write fails — leaves the edit pending and says so once. A save at a note switch, close or ⌘S whose file will not read, or whose write fails, keeps the typed text as a conflict backup under .maugham/conflicts/ and names it in the notice; when that backup cannot be written either, the notice says the edits were not saved. An edit whose note has left Research, stopped being a note, or whose path the project refuses is not dropped either: a timed autosave keeps it pending and the save at a note switch, close or ⌘S keeps it as a conflict backup and names it. A writer that reads a note to rewrite it waits for any save of that note already in flight, so it never writes text made from older bytes over the writer's edit. A note a verb is moving, renaming or trashing is never written afresh at its old path, and nothing waits on the verb (#142 T2, tripwire 14) — the Research verbs, and the Collection piece verbs that move a piece's folder with its research/ in it: a reorder (every renumbered piece's notes, across both phases of its temp-name swap) and a rename (#145; every production caller of `relocateUserContent` is classified as entering the span or holding no Research, `TripwireGrepTests.test_everyBespokeMoverCallerSaysWhetherItMovesResearch`; a piece's Delete moves only its manuscript file and leaves its research folder where it is): a save that finds the note's file missing while the note is in `ProjectStore.withResearchItemsInFlight`'s span (from just before the typed mover is called until the in-memory manifest names the new place) and is not the verb's own flush (`ResearchItemsMoving.byThisTask`, written as before) leaves a timed autosave's text pending, set again when the span ends without another keystroke, and says nothing; a flush keeps the text as a conflict backup and says “Couldn’t save “X”: it was being moved or deleted just then. Your edits were kept in the project’s .maugham/conflicts folder as “…”.” (or that they weren’t saved when the backup fails too); and any other save (the assistant, Replace, a rename sweep, a restore) is not made and says “Couldn’t save “X”: it was being moved or deleted just then.” (`NoteLookup.beingMoved`). A file missing with no verb moving it is written afresh, as before. A direct save that reads during the span of a file deleted outside Maugham before the verb began is turned away the same way. That no save waits on a verb (two review rounds found wait cycles, and a hung ⌘S or close is worse than a named backup) is the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's. A moved or renamed note's asset-reference rewrite runs after that span and BEFORE the manifest save, so a manifest save that fails still leaves the note's refs pointing at its new folder; residual: a rewrite that itself fails is logged and not shown to the writer, and the refs stay stale. Every note save re-checks, inside the coordinated write, that the file still holds the bytes the door read, as a table's does (M5-AN-084).

statement: A checkpoint revert of a figure answers its notes by ONE walk (`FigureRestoreNotePlan`, Core; the figure twin of `RewindImpact.travelStatusChanges`) with three classes, and a note is changed only where the revert rewrites its cell. STRANDED (accepted now, not accepted at the checkpoint pointer, its cell rewritten): the cell change IS the note's `claudeAcceptRevert` (cell and note in one op) and the note reopens. RETURNING (open after a Revert, accepted at the pointer, the restore writes its accepted value back): the cell change becomes a `claudeAccept` carrying the note, checkpoint-stamped, and the note returns to ACCEPTED (RULING-57 for figures). GONE (its row or column does not exist at the checkpoint): `claudeArchive`, status only, or a status-only reopen where this hand may not dispose. A note on a cell the restore does not write keeps its status, and so does a note accepted at the pointer and now (R-A, RULING-58). A revived row or column counts as written, at the value the revive gives each live cell: a stranded note there gets a status-only revert, a returning one a status-only accept. A stranded note whose cell the restore writes to that note's OWN suggested content stays accepted, whether by a cell set or a revive (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver). Where two stranded notes share the written cell the change carries the note with the newest cell-carrying accept and the other gets a status-only revert (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver). 'Accepted at the pointer' means the note's latest honoured lifecycle line at the pointer is an accept, whether or not that accept wrote a cell (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver; plan 1 final review F2, refining the next sentence). A guarded-accepted note (status-only accept, no cell-carrying accept after the pointer; M5-AN-075) that was NOT accepted at the pointer is judged by its anchor cell and suggested content: it IS stranded where the restore writes its cell away from the suggestion (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver; this overrules the design spec's section 3 sentence that such a note is never stranded). One accepted at the pointer is never stranded, whatever its cell held then (type 42, Accept status-only, edit to 7, checkpoint, edit to 9, revert: the cell goes back to 7 and the note stays accepted). The mirror: a guarded accept at the pointer, taken back since (its ⌘Z), returns to ACCEPTED when the restore writes its anchor cell back to the suggested content, by a status-only `claudeAccept` after a plain cell set (its accept never wrote a cell), not left open over its own value (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver). A restore that stops part way and is retried writes one accept for a returning note, not two.

statement: Where the cell's content already is the suggestion's content (format and alignment aside), Accept marks the note accepted and writes nothing to the cell: one status-only `claudeAccept` (`figure == nil`, `FigureAnnotationOps.statusOnlyAccept`). The check runs after every existing refusal and after the changed-since check, and `confirmChanged` makes no difference. No accept in the log ever records `prior == next` (RULING-59), including after the race that leaves a note open over its own value (a peer's reject, then a reopen). Its ⌘Z, in or out of a grid visit, is a status-only `claudeAcceptRevert` that reopens the note and moves no cell (`Change.statusOnly`); ⇧⌘Z accepts again, guarded again. The ⌘Z and ⇧⌘Z (and the visit's undo and redo) DECLINE, writing nothing, once the cell has changed or its row is gone. A restore may strand a guarded accept (M5-AN-073).

statement: Accept of a suggested change writes a status-only `claudeAccept` (no changes) in exactly these cases: (1) the note's newest text-carrying `claudeAccept` is for the note's paragraph and its `next` is the live paragraph, even when the span's quote no longer resolves; (2) the replacement stands, aligned, around the quote occurrence the span's anchor resolves to in the live paragraph, AND either (2a) the text can answer for itself (`SuggestionSplice.textCanAnswer`) or (2b) the note's own history says its splice is live. (2a), the ORDINARY shape: the note's oldest honoured text-carrying `claudeAccept` is for the note's paragraph and its `prior` (the paragraph before the suggestion was ever applied) did NOT already read as the replacement at the anchor ('dark' → 'very dark' on 'The night was dark and cold.'). Then the live text can only read as the replacement there because the suggestion, or the writer's own hand, put it there, and the span reading is consulted whatever the later history: an ordinary-shape suggestion, once applied, is never spliced twice (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver). (2b), the COINCIDENCE shape (that `prior` already read as the replacement at the anchor: the second 'dark' of 'It was dark, very dark.') and a note with no text-carrying accept at all: the text cannot answer, and the history fold decides. 'Live' is a fold over the note's honoured lifecycle lines in opId order: an accept opens it; a text-carrying revert or RULING-33 repair closes it; a status-only revert or reopen written by Maugham's own travel (stamped `.rewind` or `.undoRewind`, or with a checkpoint) closes it; every other line, every archive (a travel's own too) and every other status-only line leaves it unchanged (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver for the fold's travel arms and for a span whose splice is still in the text being accepted status-only where it used to refuse as anchor-lost); (3) the paragraph already equals the computed result (the whole-paragraph hand-typed case). Otherwise Accept splices as before, or refuses as anchor-lost (RULING-5); a span whose quote is gone while its splice is NOT in place still refuses. So no accept records a before-text equal to its after-text (RULING-59), and a suggestion is not spliced twice: after another device's newer archive or stet and a Reopen, after a restore that put the splice back following a Revert, after an edit elsewhere in the paragraph; and, for an ordinary-shape suggestion, also where the splice came back by a line that is not a lifecycle line while the fold says it was taken out: Accept → pane Revert → Archive → a rewind to after the accept → an edit elsewhere → pane Reopen → Accept; the Mac accepts, the phone reverts, and the Mac's whole-paragraph edit made before that revert arrived brings the splice back on the merge (Mac and phone alike); the race → a rewind that removes the paragraph → a return journey to after the accept → an edit elsewhere → Accept. After the writer's Revert an ordinary-shape suggestion splices again (the original text does not read as the replacement at the anchor). For a coincidence-shape suggestion, after the writer's Revert and after Maugham's own travel took the splice out (a rewind to before the accept, a rewind that removed the paragraph followed by a return journey, a checkpoint revert), Accept splices again. After the writer's reopen-only Revert of a hand-typed accept it is status-only again. The status-only accept's ⌘Z is an `annotationReopen` that leaves the text, declined, and said to the writer, once another device moved the note or another device's text-carrying accept became the note's newest, and ⇧⌘Z re-accepts, guarded again; Revert restores the original (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver). Mac and phone decide it in one Core function (tripwire 19). Known limits, each a documented limit not pinned by a test (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver): (L1) the span reading follows the anchor resolver's choice of quote occurrence; (L2) a hand-typed SPAN suggestion on a never-accepted note is spliced as written (there is no text-carrying accept to ask, and nothing in its history says a splice is live); (L3) COINCIDENCE SHAPE ONLY since the final-review fix: any route that returns the splice by a line that is not a lifecycle line while the fold is closed, followed by an edit elsewhere in the paragraph and Accept, splices the suggestion a second time. That includes the race → a rewind that removes the paragraph → a return journey to after the accept (step 9's `.rewind` reopen closes the fold); Accept → pane Revert → Archive → a rewind to after the accept → an edit elsewhere → pane Reopen; and the two-device burst (Mac accepts, phone reverts, the Mac's older-context whole-paragraph edit returns the splice on merge). The result is visible and ⌘Z takes it back; (L4) COINCIDENCE SHAPE ONLY, the opposite failure: accept → a rewind that removes the paragraph (a travel archive, neutral in the fold) → pane Reopen of the archived row (unstamped, leaves the fold live) → a return journey to before the accept → Accept: the fold says live and the untouched text already reads as the replacement at the anchor, so Accept marks the note accepted and writes nothing. An ordinary-shape suggestion on that route splices, since its original text does not read as the replacement.

statement: A Research table's save knows which save it is (`ResearchTableHost.SaveSource`: the debounced timer, a flush, or a direct write by the assistant or Restore) and answers with what it did (`WriteOutcome`); the host is left clean only when the save wrote. The debounced save, refused for any reason, writes nothing over the file, leaves the host unsaved (the edit waits for a later save) and says why, once for each refused save (a later debounced save refused again says it again): the version cannot be kept, the file will not read, the item has left Research, the path is outside a research root, the outside version cannot be backed up, the save fails, or the file is gone (the file is not made again). Where the host used to forget the edit on item-gone, outside-Research and file-gone, it now stays unsaved (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver). A write by the assistant or a Restore, and the save it makes first of the writer's pending edits, are not flushes: their refusals are unchanged and still answer as before (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver); a refused pre-flush stops the assistant's write with "The table’s unsaved edits couldn’t be saved first, so the change wasn’t made. Don’t send it again; ask the writer to save or reopen the table.", the writer's edit alone stays in the table and nothing is written.

When the save itself fails at close, the table's edits are written as a backup copy under .maugham/conflicts and the notice names the file. Reading Denver's "at close" as every flush, so that ⌘S and leaving the grid are included and only the debounced save still refuses, is the notes' own split (`ResearchNoteDoor.SaveSource`), ruled as built (Denver, 2026-11-11, P3, RULING-24's amendment; RULING-60 inherits it). scope: ResearchTableHost.write — what a flush does where it cannot save
statement: Where a flush cannot save a Research table, it writes nothing over the file, keeps the held table's CSV as an unsaved backup under .maugham/conflicts and names it (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver, throughout this claim except where it says ruled: that a flush saves anyway, P3, and that a failed save at close is backed up and named, RULING-60, M5-AN-081). Each arm says its own sentence once (X is the item's title, K is " Your edits were kept in the project’s .maugham/conflicts folder as “<file>”."): the file will not read, "Couldn’t save “X”: Maugham couldn’t read it to keep its previous version." + K; the item has left Research, "Couldn’t save a Research table: it is no longer in Research." + K; the path is outside a research root, "Couldn’t save “X”: it isn’t a table inside Research any more." + K; the outside version cannot be backed up (the outside bytes stay, no version is kept), "Couldn’t save “X”: it changed outside Maugham, and that version couldn’t be kept." + K; the save fails, "Couldn’t save “X”: <error>" + K; the file is gone, "Couldn’t save “X”: it isn’t there any more." + K, and the file is not made again, a change from an earlier deliberate 'dropped and said'. If the backup cannot be written either, the notice ends "Your edits weren’t saved, and they couldn’t be kept anywhere else." The backup is named from the item's own .csv path, else from research/table.csv. A flush on a clean host keeps nothing and says nothing. After a flush keeps the edits aside the host STAYS UNSAVED and remembers what it kept (the hash of the CSV text and the backup file): a later flush, or the close, tries the file again with the same table and says nothing more, and if the file can then be written the edits are on disk with no second backup; an assistant write is refused meanwhile ("The table’s unsaved edits couldn’t be saved first, so the change wasn’t made. Don’t send it again; ask the writer to save or reopen the table."), so the writer's edits are never stamped as the assistant's; an outside change does not reload over the held table; a later edit keeps a second backup at its own flush; a remembered backup that has gone is kept again and said. A backup that fails is said once and retried silently, and the flush that can then keep it names it. The memory is cleared when a write lands or the host reloads. After a flush's backup the writer may close with the table still unsaved: the edits are in the backup, which was named once. Moved here from M5-AN-081 (that a flush saves anyway is ruled as built, P3, RULING-60 inheriting it; the notice's wording and its being said once, after the save has landed, are the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver): a flush that saves though the previous version could not be kept says so once, after the save has landed, "“X”’s previous version couldn’t be kept; your edits were saved anyway."; nothing is kept aside and the host ends clean. The backup is named <stem>-<itemId>-unsaved-<stamp>.csv and holds the table's CSV with the file's separator, line ending and byte-order mark, and no sidecar formats. A close that finds the edits already saved or kept says nothing more: one backup and one notice on the way out, through the store's flush then the release, and a grid's leave then its release. Background flushes (the search debounce, Replace, a promotion, add_note, a note switch, the typed mover) are flushes too, as they are for notes (the notes' save-anyway rule, ruled as built, P3).
intent: INTENTIONAL — the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver, except that a flush saves anyway (ruled as built, P3) and the close's backup is RULING-60's (spec 'Calls made here' and plan 2's rulings P2-5 and P2-6; P2-6 overrules the spec's sentence that a backup leaves the host clean)

statement: A Research table's host is registered only by the first caller back from the opening that read it, at which point no one has held it; the store never registers a closing or closed host, replaces a closed entry in the registry, and hands every caller of one opening the one live registered host, counting exactly one use per successful return. Open it again."), a bound that is coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver. An opening that throws leaves no registry entry and no use. Giving back a host that is not the registered one is a no-op. No holder's release ever skips the host's close, and the close flushes, so no edit is lost between an opening and a release.

statement: A Research table's save and a Research note's save each re-check, inside the coordinated write and before writing, that the file still holds the bytes the door read (`FileExpectation`: `.bytesHashing(ContentHash.of(bytes read))`, or `.absent` where the note door read no file; a read that finds the note missing while a verb is moving it never reaches `.absent`, M5-AN-070); a mismatch writes nothing and throws `FileSaveError.changedSinceRead`. Applying the check to the note door as well as the table's is the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver. The door then goes round once more from its read (a second pass, not a copy): the new bytes are kept as a version and, for a table, as an outside backup, then the save is made against them, and the table's usual notice follows once: "“X” changed outside Maugham while you were editing it. That version is kept in .maugham/conflicts/<file>; yours was saved." (or "Those versions are kept in .maugham/conflicts/A and .maugham/conflicts/B; yours was saved." where a pending backup was also named). A note's save of the writer's own edit (editor timer or flush) that keeps outside bytes as a version now says the same once, after the save lands: "“X” changed outside Maugham while you were editing it. That version is kept in its Versions; yours was saved." (RULING-62, M5-AN-089; the assistant's direct saves keep the bytes silently). The note door's wait, read and ask-again loop (`ResearchNoteDoor.fileMayHaveChanged`) is a twin of `ResearchTableHost.fileMayHaveChanged()`, not shared code. A note whose file was absent at the read and made outside before the write is kept the same way. A caller that made its text from its own read of the note (Search & Replace) also hands the door that read's hash (`saveResearchNote(expectingBytesHash:)`, SHA-256 of the bytes it read; every other caller passes nil and is unchanged): when the bytes the door reads, on its first read or its retry, are not those, the door writes nothing, keeps nothing, says nothing, and answers `.changedSinceTheCallerRead`, which Replace turns into `staleSearchMatch` (#147 R2; compare-and-swap, the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-17, not Denver's). The manuscript's clean render is not checked (`.anything`).

scope: DocumentStore.settleResearchTable / ProjectStore.useInDocument, bringBack — a stale table is not used
statement: Before Use in Document or Bring Back to Figures reads a Research table's file, the grid open on it is settled (its open edit committed, its pending save flushed), and `DocumentStore.settleResearchTable` answers whether the file now holds what the grid shows: true when no grid has the table open or its host is clean after the settle, false when the flush kept the edits aside (the host is still unsaved, or closed so). When it is false both verbs refuse before reading the file and write nothing — no figure is made, nothing is appended to the parked figure's log — throwing once "X has edits that couldn't be saved, so it wasn't used. Try again once the table can be saved." (`UseInDocumentRefused.unsavedEdits`) or "X has edits that couldn't be saved, so it wasn't brought back. Try again once the table can be saved." (`FigureReturnRefused.unsavedEdits`), X the item's title. Once the table can be saved, the same verb saves it and goes on with what the grid shows. Moving a Research table to the Trash settles it too and goes on whatever the answer: the item is leaving, and edits that could not be written are in the backup the flush named. All of it is the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver.

scope: ResearchTableHost.fileMayHaveChanged / reloadUnlessEdited — no reload over a write in flight
statement: A Research table open in a grid is never replaced by the file's outside version while a save of it is in flight or has begun since the file was read for the reload. `fileMayHaveChanged` waits for every save asked, one queued behind the save it saw at entry included, before it asks whether the grid is clean; a reload that a write overtook (the host's write-in-flight flag is set, or a write began after the reload read the file) replaces nothing, and is asked again once that write has ended, so an outside change that lands after the write is still read and said ("Reloaded “X” — the file changed outside Maugham."). The outside bytes the write found are kept by the save itself (a conflict backup and a version) before the writer's table is written. Before this the grid could end showing the outside table while the file held the writer's, with the host clean. All of it is the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver.

scope: QuitCoordinator / MaughamAppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate — ⌘Q waits for the stores to close
statement: When the app is asked to quit, it defers termination until every open project's stores have closed — the figure windows' last writes, then `DocumentStore.close()`, which flushes every pending save, a Research table's and a note's included (`ProjectSessionRegistry.quitClosers` → `ProjectSession.closeForQuit`), and any close already in flight is waited for — and then lets the quit go; with no project open the quit is immediate. The wait is bounded at ten seconds: stores that have not closed by then are left and the app quits anyway, never a hung quit. A second quit request while one is pending starts no second round, and the quit is let go exactly once. The quit coordinator is the only code that closes the stores at quit: the project window's own quit arm, which started a close nothing waited for, is gone. A test host is never held. The update paths are unchanged: Restart & Update's helper waits for the process to exit, and a dismissed staged update is handed to the helper at willTerminate, after the stores have closed. A quit the app asks for itself (Restart & Update; the test MCP's quit tool) goes through `MaughamAppDelegate.requestQuit`, the one production call of `NSApp.terminate`, which hands the call to the run loop (`RunLoop.main.perform`): AppKit spins a run loop inside `terminate` while the quit is deferred, a run loop nested in a main-queue block does not drain the main queue, and so a `terminate` called from a main-actor task could never hear its reply — neither the closers nor the ten-second bound ran. 0.46.0 and 0.47.0 shipped that: Restart & Update with a project open left the app half-quit, with nothing loading or saving, until it was force-quit. RULING-60 names quit as a close; the deferral, its bound and its shape are the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver.
intent: INTENTIONAL — the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver (plan 2 final review, G1)
reachability: LIVE — ⌘Q, Quit from the menu or the Dock, log out or restart, and Restart & Update, with a project open
known_gaps: The AppKit half is not driven by any test: that AppKit asks the delegate, honours .terminateLater and quits on the reply is asserted only by the delegate's answer function and by reading the source (the adaptor is installed, the reply is made). It needs the manual smoke (type in a Research table, ⌘Q at once, reopen: the edit is there). test_aQuitTheAppAsksForFromATaskStillHearsItsReply stands in for AppKit's nested loop with its own (it went red, unanswered at its three seconds, with `terminate` called straight from the task); the real Restart & Update with a project open is not driven by any test and is the release's manual check. While the quit is deferred the windows are still on screen over stores that are closing; nothing tested says a keystroke in that window of time is refused or kept. Likewise an MCP write or a compile ingest into a project whose store has already closed, while the coordinator still waits on another project's close, is not waited for (unpinned). A save that fails at quit is kept in .maugham/conflicts, but its notice goes to a window that is closing, so the writer is not told; past the ten-second bound the app quits with only a log line.

scope: add_note — the Palette group is not a destination
statement: The MCP tool add_note refuses the Palette group as its parent: when parent_group_id is the group `PaletteLookup.paletteGroup(in:)` finds (role-first, whatever the writer has renamed it) it throws invalidArgument "The Palette holds the writer's cards; add_note can't create one. Add the note to another Research group." before anything is created — no item, no file. It still adds a note with no parent or in any other group. Only the Palette group itself is refused: a subgroup beneath the Palette is not, and what is added there is a note (`ResearchTextRole.of` is role-first: a document in a subgroup beneath the Palette is a note, a card is a direct child of the group); where such a note lands on disk follows `addResearchTextNote`'s folder from the parent's title slug (`research/<subgroup slug>/`), the spec's already-filed low finding (same root cause: the folder comes from the parent's title slug, not its path; the spec's case is a renamed-and-deduped group, this one a subgroup). The tool's own description says it cannot add to the Palette. The assistant therefore never creates a card (RULING-61); update_note refuses a card (M5-AN-072).

scope: ResearchNoteDoor.fileMayHaveChanged — an open note or card hears an outside change
statement: A Research note or palette card hears a change made outside Maugham (another device syncing, an external editor) the way a table does, by the window's file presenter (`DocumentStore.researchFileMayHaveChanged` → `researchNoteItem(atPath:)`, compared without case → `ResearchNoteDoor.fileMayHaveChanged`), by this table: (1) an item no editor holds open (`holdResearchNoteOpen`, held by the note editor's and the card editor's `.task(id:)` and released when it switches or goes — the hold is one suspension ended only by the task's cancellation, raised and lowered once each on every exit, even for a task cancelled before it starts), or whose bytes nobody here has read, hears nothing and says nothing; the next save still keeps the outside bytes as a version. (2) bytes the door last read or wrote (its own save coming back, a BOM note read as it is) are no change. (3) Other bytes with nothing pending: they become the known bytes, the writer's run ends, the open editor reloads, and "Reloaded “X” — the file changed outside Maugham." is posted. A save in flight is waited for and the file asked about again; so is a save, edit or read that began (even one that ended) during the door's own read, the bytes read predating it. (4) Other bytes with an edit pending: the edit is left alone; its save (editor timer or flush) keeps those bytes as a version and posts once, after the write lands, "“X” changed outside Maugham while you were editing it. That version is kept in its Versions; yours was saved."; if the writer typed before a reload landed, the save that covers those bytes says it too. The assistant's and other direct saves keep outside bytes as a version without that notice. Where each case is said (at the save's landing, not when the change is heard), the stale-read guard, the open-only hold and "where to find it" being the item's Versions are the coordinator's calls, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's; the two cases themselves are RULING-62's. Known residual as built (50a6b35b): if the writer types between the "Reloaded" notice and the editor's re-read, the editor keeps the writer's text (the re-read is skipped while an edit is pending), so "Reloaded" was said a moment early; the save that then covers the outside bytes (`reloadedFromOutside`) keeps them as a version and posts the "while you were editing it" notice once (`outsideKeptForTheWriter`), pinned by `ResearchNoteDoorTests.test_typingBeforeAnOutsideReloadLandsIsSaidWhenItsSaveKeepsTheOutsideBytes`. The door's loop is a twin of `ResearchTableHost.fileMayHaveChanged()`, not shared code.
intent: INTENTIONAL — ruled 2026-11-16 (RULING-62); the build's timing and guards are coordinator's calls, not Denver's

scope: ProjectStore.replaceMatch / replaceAll — a Research file's match is re-found in the text just read, and a stale match, or one whose occurrences changed since the search, is refused
statement: Research Replace never splices at the search-time character offsets, and a stale match is refused. A single Replace of a Research note, card or other research file takes the clicked match's ordinal among its document's matches in the current search (`ordinal(of:)`, the one helper both the research and the manuscript arm use) and replaces that occurrence in the text it has just read, after the flush and the settle of the editor's pending edit (`replacingResearchMatches`), so an edit made since the search, or an earlier Replace, does not move the replacement. Both arms re-find the clicked occurrence by one rule (`ClickedOccurrence.range`), with the search engine's own matcher (`ProjectSearchEngine.matchesIn`), checking the text the search read — a manuscript's display form, which is the text replaced in, or a note's `MarkdownDisplayFilter.stripAnchors(stored)`: the count check refuses when that text holds a different number of occurrences than the document's matches in the current results (one added or removed since the search), and the line check refuses when the occurrence at the ordinal shows a different line (`linePreview`) or place in it (`matchRangeInLine`) than the clicked result (one added and another removed, or an edit on the clicked line); where a note's stored text differs from what the search read (`\r\n` line endings, edge whitespace, an anchor-shaped line), the same matcher runs over the stored text and the occurrence at the same ordinal is replaced there, refused unless that count is the expected one too, so a Replace in a Windows-line-ending note or on a note's whitespace-edged first or last line lands in place and an anchor-shaped line holding the query is refused; an edit elsewhere that leaves the occurrences and the clicked line alone still replaces the clicked one. A match whose id is not in the current results (they were refreshed since its results, by a Replace or a search) means the one current match with the same path, range and line preview (`listedMatch(for:)`, #147 R1) only when its document is unchanged since the click's results — those results (the last 8 that landed, `recentlyLandedSearches`) are for the same query and options and list the same occurrences (range, line, place in it) in that document as the current ones — and the clicked-occurrence check runs on it as usual: another document's match still shown after a Replace is replaced, and of two matches on identical lines there the old click names the one with its range, never the other; in a document a Replace (or an edit) has changed since, the stale click is refused, since an identical line at its old range may be another occurrence. A match with no such current match, or several, or whose results are no longer remembered, or one either check refuses, throws ProjectStoreError.staleSearchMatch (“That match has changed. Search again.”) and writes nothing, in both arms (the research arm's unsafe-path and not-Research refusals still come first); every such refusal (or failure once the occurrence is being re-found) refreshes the results. A successful single Replace and a Replace All each end by refreshing the current results undebounced (searching what the field last asked for), so the results a caller reads once it returns are fresh, and a match value from before is refused unless a current match has its path, range and line. Single Replaces and Replace All run one at a time through one chain (`takingTheReplaceTurn`), each waiting for the one issued before it and its refresh: two quick clicks on the same match replace once (the second is refused), a single Replace issued after a Replace All is judged against fresh results, and a Replace that throws still ends its turn. A search lands only if it started after the last one that landed (`searchGeneration`), so an older search finishing after a Replace's refresh is dropped, and `clearSearch` drops any search still in flight. Replace All replaces every occurrence of the query that the text just read holds, not the search-time list, and a file whose query is gone since the search is skipped with nothing written. A note's write is compare-and-swap (#147 R2, M5-AN-084): Replace hands the door the hash of the bytes it read, and a note changed (outside Maugham) after that read is not written and keeps no version: a single Replace throws staleSearchMatch (and refreshes the results), and Replace All skips that note, names it in `leftAlone` with the documents it already leaves alone, and replaces the rest. That Replace re-finds by ordinal, falls back by path, range and line for a missing id, refuses a stale match, checks the count and the clicked line, runs one at a time, that Replace All takes its turn, and the refresh after each, are the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's
intent: INTENTIONAL — the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's
reachability: LIVE — Search & Replace over a Research note after typing in it, after a first Replace, after Replace All, or with a double click on one match
fix_history: Statement rewritten 2026-11-16 (hardening 11-16 plan 2, Task 8): the helper is `ordinal(of:)`, the stale error is `.staleSearchMatch` (was “Match range out of bounds”), and two Replaces in a row no longer name the following occurrence: the second is refused (#141 follow-up, 7407bf5b and 231d60c0). Final fix wave 2026-11-16 (whole-branch review I1): an occurrence added before the clicked one made the ordinal name another occurrence; the count and line checks now refuse it, an edit on the clicked line is refused (was: replaced; `test_replaceMatchAfterAnEditInsertedBeforeItReplacesTheMatch_notTheOldOffsets` became `test_replaceAfterAnEditOnTheClickedOccurrencesLineIsRefused`), and these refusals refresh the results. Correction the same day (final re-review): the research arm's check read the stored text while the search read its `stripAnchors` form, so a single Replace always refused in a `\r\n` note and on a whitespace-edged first or last line; the checks now read the text the search read and the replace lands in the stored text by the same ordinal. Hardening 2026-11-17 (Task 4, #147 R1): every Replace refreshed the results and minted new ids, so a click on another document's still-shown match was refused (“That match has changed”) though nothing had changed, and a refusal for a missing id left the results unrefreshed; a missing id now falls back to the one current match with the same path, range and line preview (none or several is a refusal), and every staleSearchMatch refusal refreshes the results. Hardening 2026-11-17 (Task 5, #147 R2): a note changed outside Maugham between Replace's read and the door's write was kept as a version and written over silently; Replace now passes its read's hash to the door (compare-and-swap) and a mismatch is a stale match (single Replace) or a skipped, named note (Replace All). The coordinator's call, not Denver's. Fix round 1 the same day (task review): the fallback could name another occurrence in the document the earlier Replace changed (identical lines, ranges shifted); it now applies only where the document's occurrences are unchanged since the click's results.

scope: ResearchVersionStore.prune(sparing:) — a restore spares the version it restores
statement: A restore through a door spares the version it restores. Each door's keep (`keepThePriorVersion`, the note door's and `ResearchTableHost`'s) prunes this device's versions past the newest 50 sparing `ResearchVersionStore.sparing(made:restoring:)` — the version the keep just made and, for a restore, the version being restored (the doors' `restoring:` is that version's file name, nil when the save is not a restore) — so restoring the oldest of fifty keeps it until the write has landed, and a restore whose write fails leaves it on disk. The names spared count toward the 50: the count stays at 50. The note door and the table door ask the one function, so they cannot spare differently. Sparing the restored version is the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's.

scope: add_note and promote_inbox_entry (a text capture) — the body goes through the note door as the assistant
statement: With a DocumentStore wired, add_note writes its body, and an MCP promote_inbox_entry of a text capture writes the capture's text, to the note it has just created through the note door as the assistant (`saveResearchNote(by: .assistant)`; the promotion passes `by: .assistant`, the app's own Promote to Research the writer), so the writer's first edit of it keeps the assistant's text as a version marked as the assistant's. The write must land: when the door's save does not, the call throws `researchTextNotSaved` before the inbox flip — the capture stays in the inbox — and first takes back the empty note it created just before (`ProjectStore.takeBackUnsavedNewNote`; a kept letter does the same, M5-AN-070; #148 D1): the row and its file leave through the ordinary delete path, trashed by id and then permanently deleted, so no Trash entry is left and ⌘⌥Z is not armed, and a kept letter's link to its chapter goes with it; a retried promotion makes one note. Only that note's row and file go (its id is fresh and its file was minted beside any note of the same title), so a note the writer already had is untouched. A new file that holds bytes when the save is refused (written outside Maugham meanwhile) is not the empty note and is left: the error is the refusal with “; the note “<title>” was left in Research because its file changed outside Maugham.” in place of its full stop. A cleanup that itself fails leaves the note too, and the error ends “; the empty note “<title>” was left in Research.” Taking the note back, and leaving one that holds bytes, are the coordinator's calls, hardening 2026-11-17, not Denver's. With no DocumentStore ever wired the body is written raw and keeps nothing; a store that lost its DocumentStore refuses (`noteWriteRefusedAsTheProjectCloses`), never raw (M5-AN-070). Recording these as the assistant's, and the throw before the flip, are coordinator's calls, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's.
